main_text.l: tyropolitanus Metropolita & Locumtenens,
& Elias piissimus Presbyter & Locumtenens,
Cosmas[?] item Apocrisiarius Alexandrini dixere;
Hoc Ecclesiasticis Canonibus non adversatur;
Nanque Alexandrinus, & Patriarchalis thro-
nus Antiochenus, & similiter sancta Civitatis,
in quocunque ordine sive seculari, sive clericali
invenerint virtute reliquis aliys praestantiorem,
ad archieraticam sedem promovere non dedi-
gnantur: neque enim ob solos Clericos Christus
in terram descendit, neque illis solis virtutis
praemia circumduxit, sed universo Christiano-
rum complemento. Hoc itaque si approbatum
fuerit receptumque, omnes Archieraticae sedes
in desolationem atque interitum abibunt. Potior
enim eorum pars, quae apud nostros inclaruit,
ex laicali ordine ad Archieraticas sedes evecti
sunt. Nos huic assensum praebere non possu-
mus, ne contra nostros Praesules sententiam tu-
lisse deprehendamur: Sancta Synodus dixit;
Singulae sedes habent singulares suas proprias
consuetudines, neque pro iis cum aliis in contro-
versiam veniendum est, & decertandum. Obser-
vat siquidem Romana Ecclesia suas consuetu-
dines, quod & convenit. Observat itidem
& Constantinopolitana Ecclesia quasdam suas con-
suetudines ab antiquo tempore sibi traditas,
similiter & throni Orientales. Quare si Roma-
na Ecclesia nunquam ex laico in Praesulem
admi-

page.notes: The name at the start of the second line is printed as "Cofmas" or "Cosmas"; I read it as Cosmas but it is doubtful. The first line's word "Tyropolitanus" begins the page as a fragment, so the first paragraph is marked cont="true". The left edge shows stray marks and fragments of the neighbouring page; these were left out. The word "aliys" is printed as such and kept. Spelling of u/v was normalised as instructed; printed punctuation spacing (for example before commas) was kept only where it did not affect the words.
